items.item_text: resume
cover letter
High school diploma or equivalent experience
Experience using computerized scheduling systems, information retrieval, and data entry
One year clerical experience in a medical setting using computerized practice management systems and multiple phone line systems
Demonstrated experience reviewing data from multiple information systems, including insurance carrier and broker websites
Experience changing computerized practice management clinician schedules
Experience working on multiple tasks concurrently with frequent interruptions
Experience processing insurance referrals, denied claims, and eligibility

Under the direct supervision of the Clerical Support Supervisor, the Patient Support/Insurance Assistant performs a wide variety of tasks in the areas of reception, appointment scheduling, insurance, and billing.

Primary functional areas of responsibility vary depending on operational need within Student Health Services (SHS), which may dictate any combination of duties, utilizing medical background and training, and in accordance with department policies. Each position is cross-trained in all areas to provide backup support and primary coverage as needed.
Sensitivity to ethnic, cultural, and lifestyle diversity
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.
Selected candidate will be required to take a TB test within 60 days of hire.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

Will be required to comply with current Student Health Center employee health safety requirements for health care workers as defined by state and federal regulatory agencies. Current health safety requirements are discussed during interview.
The selected candidate will be required to work all scheduled hours on-site.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Customer-oriented, with the ability to listen and anticipate the needs of customers and to respond quickly to customer problems
Complete Health Insurance Portability and Accessibility (HIPAA) training within 30 days of hire.
Demonstrated knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, and diagnostic tests
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
Demonstrated knowledge of medical records management
Demonstrated ability to operate miscellaneous office equipment including PC
Excellent written communication skills
Excellent oral communication skills with the ability to provide complex, detailed information clearly and concisely to a diverse population
Demonstrated ability to identify, research, and resolve complex problems
Close attention to detail with the ability to proofread work carefully
Demonstrated exceptional organizational skills to ensure tasks are completed quickly and accurately

Excellent listening skills with the ability to work and communicate positively and cooperatively with management and supervisory staff, medical staff, co-workers, other healthcare personnel, patients, and their families when providing information and services, seeking assistance and clarification, and resolving problems
Ability to handle difficult, sensitive, and confidential situations tactfully with accuracy, timeliness, confidentiality, and sensitivity
